about.title: About
about.about_body: Crisis Reporter is a community-driven damage reporting platform built for UNDP. It enables rapid infrastructure assessment following sudden-onset disasters, helping UNDP coordinate crisis response faster and more effectively.
about.how_body: Reporters submit photos and damage assessments from the field. UNDP staff review and verify reports on the dashboard. Verified data is exported for crisis response coordination with partner organisations.
about.version_note: Crisis Reporter is built for UNDP's InnoCentive Crisis Mapping Challenge

tandc.title: Terms & Conditions
tandc.subtitle: Please read and accept to continue
tandc.body:
By using Crisis Reporter, you agree to our Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy.

Crisis Reporter collects location data, photos, and description information to support UNDP crisis response operations. Your data is stored securely and shared only with authorised UNDP staff.

You may submit reports anonymously or with a verified profile. Your Reporter ID is assigned to your device and persists across sessions.

By tapping I Agree, you confirm that you have read and understood these terms and consent to the collection and use of your data as described.

You may withdraw at any time by uninstalling the app.
tandc.declineAlertMessage: You are unable to access Crisis Reporter without accepting the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy. If you change your mind, please reopen the app and try again.

welcomeCard.body: Crisis Reporter helps you document damage to buildings and infrastructure after a disaster. You can report earthquakes, floods, conflicts, and other crises. Your reports help UNDP get help to the right places faster.

earthquake.name: Earthquake
earthquake.description: Structural damage from ground shaking and tremors.

flood.name: Flood
flood.description: Water damage from overflow, heavy rain, or storm surge.

tsunami.name: Tsunami
tsunami.description: Coastal damage from large ocean waves following seismic events.

hurricane_cyclone.name: Hurricane or Cyclone
hurricane_cyclone.description: Wind and rain damage from tropical storms.

wildfire.name: Wildfire
wildfire.description: Fire damage to buildings and infrastructure.

explosion.name: Explosion
explosion.description: Blast damage from industrial or other explosive events.

chemical_incident.name: Chemical Incident
chemical_incident.description: Damage or hazard from chemical spill or release.

conflict.name: Conflict
conflict.description: Damage from armed conflict or military activity.

civil_unrest.name: Civil Unrest
civil_unrest.description: Damage from protests, riots, or civil disturbance.

guidelines.title: Photo guidelines
guidelines.g1: Make sure the damage is clearly visible in the photo
guidelines.g2: Avoid photos that are too dark or blurry
guidelines.g3: Take the photo from a safe distance — do not put yourself at risk
guidelines.g4: Include the full structure in the frame where possible

q1.title: How bad is the damage?
q1.opt_minimal: Minimal / No damage — structurally sound and functional, showing only cosmetic or no visible damage
q1.opt_partial: Partially damaged — repairable, and remains usable with caution
q1.opt_complete: Completely damaged — structurally unsafe or destroyed

q2.title: What type of infrastructure is this?
q2.opt_commercial: Commercial Infrastructure — markets, malls, shops, hotels, banks, industries, etc.
q2.opt_government: Government Building — administrative buildings, courthouses, police stations, fire stations, etc.
q2.opt_utility: Utility Infrastructure — water pumps, power plants, waste treatment plants, etc.
q2.opt_transport: Transport and Communication Infrastructure — roads, cell towers, bridges, railway station, bus station, etc.
q2.opt_community: Community Infrastructure — schools, hospitals, community halls, public toilets, etc.
q2.opt_public_spaces: Public Spaces / Recreation Infrastructure — stadiums, playgrounds, religious buildings, etc.

q3.title: Name or details of the infrastructure
q3.placeholder: Enter the name or description of the building or structure

q4.title: What type of disaster is this?

q5.title: Is there debris that needs clearing near this location?

q6.title: What is the current condition of electricity infrastructure in your community following the crisis?
q6.opt_minor: Minor damage — service disruptions but quickly repairable
q6.opt_moderate: Moderate damage — partial outages requiring repairs
q6.opt_severe: Severe damage — major infrastructure damaged, prolonged outages
q6.opt_destroyed: Completely destroyed — no electricity infrastructure functioning

q7.title: How would you rate the overall functioning of health services in your community since the event?

q8.title: What are the most pressing needs?
q8.opt_food_water: Food assistance and safe drinking water
q8.opt_healthcare: Access to healthcare and essential medicines
q8.opt_shelter: Shelter, housing repair, or temporary accommodation
q8.opt_livelihoods: Restoration of livelihoods or income sources
q8.opt_wash: Water, sanitation, and hygiene (toilets, washing facilities)
q8.opt_basic_services: Restoration of basic services and infrastructure (electricity, roads, schools)
q8.opt_local_support: Support from local authorities and community organizations

faq_m.q1_answer: Crisis Reporter is a UNDP tool that lets community members document damage to buildings and infrastructure after a disaster. Your reports help UNDP direct emergency resources to the right places faster.
faq_m.q2_question: Do I need internet to submit a report?
faq_m.q2_answer: You can fill in your report offline. Your text answers and GPS location are saved to your device. Photos require an internet connection to upload. When you reconnect, your report will send automatically.
faq_m.q3_question: How do I enable GPS on my device?
faq_m.q3_answer: On Android: go to Settings → Location and turn it on. Then open Crisis Reporter and try again. If the app still cannot access your location, go to Settings → Apps → Crisis Reporter → Permissions and enable Location.
faq_m.q4_answer: Anonymous reports contain no personal information. If you create a verified account with an email or phone number, that contact information is stored securely and shared only with authorised UNDP staff.
faq_m.q5_question: How do I know my report was received?
faq_m.q5_answer: After submission you will see a confirmation screen with your report reference number. You can also view all your submitted reports in the My Reports section.
faq_m.q6_question: How do I earn a Safety Training badge?
faq_m.q6_answer: Complete all three parts of Safety Tips — Part A covers all 9 disaster types, Part B covers reporting guidelines, Part C covers first aid. Then add an email or phone number to your profile. The badge is awarded automatically.
faq_m.q7_question: What if my country is not in the list?
faq_m.q7_answer: Crisis Reporter is currently operational in countries where UNDP is actively responding to a crisis. If your country is not listed it means UNDP has not yet activated it. Check back during an active crisis event.
faq_m.q8_question: Can I edit a report after submitting it?
faq_m.q8_answer: Reports cannot be edited after submission. If you need to update information, you can submit a new report for the same location. UNDP staff will see all reports for a location and consider the most recent.
faq_m.q9_question: What do the damage levels mean?
faq_m.q9_answer: Minimal or No Damage: the building is structurally sound with only cosmetic damage. Partially Damaged: the building is repairable but should be used with caution. Completely Destroyed: the building is structurally unsafe.
faq_m.q10_answer: Yes. All data is transmitted over encrypted connections and stored securely. Photos are anonymised before storage. Your personal details are never shared with third parties.
faq_m.q11_question: How do I contact UNDP about a report?
faq_m.q11_answer: Crisis Reporter is for damage documentation only. For emergency assistance, contact your local emergency services. For questions about UNDP operations in your area, visit undp.org.
